h1:
Rayong Mookata & BBQ Buffet
10 Great-Value Dinner Spots
intro: One of the most common dinners locals in Rayong meet up for is mookata — Thai BBQ where you gather around a dome grill, cook for hours, refill all you want, and pay only a couple hundred baht a head. Rayong has everything from buffets just over 100 THB a head to places that bring out a full line of premium beef and seafood. We've picked 10 spots that locals actually go to, with the area, rough price, and opening hours.

blocks.html: Mookata in Rayong comes in two main styles. The first is the open-line buffet — pay once, then help yourself to pork, beef, seafood, snacks, and dessert. Most run 199–279 THB a head, and many have no time limit. The second is Korean BBQ / yakiniku ordered by the plate, better if you want to pick good cuts of meat yourself; these mostly open from evening to late. We've sorted from the lighter-priced spots up to the more loaded ones, finishing with the order-by-the-plate places.

blocks.text: Mookata & BBQ buffet spots locals in Rayong go to

items.name: Aroi Jaeng Riverside Mookata (Taling Chan Floating Market)
items.blurb: The cheapest mookata buffet on this list, sitting right by the water at Taling Chan Floating Market with an easygoing vibe. There's marinated pork, chicken, bacon, shrimp, squid, plus snacks like larb, pad thai, and som tam. Kids under 120 cm get a special rate, so it's great for the whole family.
items.meta: Taling Chan Floating Market · Open daily 16:30–23:00

items.name: 4 Mong Hot-Pan Buffet (Rayong branch)
items.blurb: A grill buffet with a low starting price. What people like is the fresh shrimp and refillable seafood; there's pork, beef, and a full spread of snacks and dessert too. Good for groups who want seafood without paying a lot. Opens in the afternoon.

items.name: Rama 9 Grilled Shrimp Korean BBQ (Noen Phra)
items.blurb: A grill buffet where grilled shrimp is the star. There's pork belly, beef, squid, bacon, and liver to grill, at a budget price. It opens a bit later, so it's handy if you finish work late.
items.meta: Sukhumvit Rd, Noen Phra · Open daily 16:00–23:00

items.name: Je Jai Dee Mookata Buffet, Butter-Grilled Kho Khun Beef
items.blurb: For grain-fed (kho khun) beef grilled with butter on a hot pan — people drive all the way out to Ban Khai for it. The food line is loaded, with salmon yam and refillable beef snacks. Budget-friendly but the ingredients are solid, and it's a place people come back to often. No time limit.
items.meta: Nong Taphan, Ban Khai district · Open daily 16:00–23:00

items.name: Thao Kae Mookata & Seafood Buffet (Saeng Chan Beach)
items.blurb: A mookata buffet right by the Saeng Chan Beach area. The highlight is fresh seafood — shrimp, shellfish, crab, and salmon. If you're staying near the beach and want dinner close to your hotel, this one's convenient. It opens earlier on weekends.
items.meta: Saeng Chan Beach area · Mon–Fri 15:30–23:00 / Sat–Sun 15:00–23:00

items.name: Tid Mun Hot-Pan Grill Buffet (Rayong branch)
items.blurb: A grill buffet locals talk about a lot, combining butter-grill, mookata, and shabu in one place. The food line is long, and you can keep refilling snacks and dessert. Good for coming as a group and settling in for a while. No time limit.
items.meta: Noen Phra, Rat Bamrung Rd (lower road) · Open 16:00–23:00

items.name: Jack Cup Korean BBQ (Choeng Noen)
items.blurb: A Korean-style pork grill buffet in the Choeng Noen area, with grilled pork and baked seafood. The price already includes drinks, so it's easy to work out the per-head cost — good if you don't want a drinks charge added on later.

items.name: Mana Shabu & Grill
items.blurb: A spot that covers both shabu and grilling in one meal. The food line is long, with imported beef and several broths, plus snacks like roast-duck jade noodles and spaghetti. If you want both hot-pot dipping and grilling done in one place, this is a great pick. Some branches open until late.
items.meta: In Rayong town · Open midday–late (check the branch)

items.name: CoCo Yakiniku
items.blurb: A Japanese-style yakiniku beef-grill spot ordered à la carte, with a garden feel. The beef comes in several grades — grain-fed kho khun, Australian, Thai wagyu, and Charolais. Good if you want to pick good cuts by the plate rather than a buffet.

items.name: Ba Korean Grill (Ban Chang)
items.blurb: A Korean BBQ spot in the Ban Chang area, ordered by set. The highlight is marinated pork belly and Korean side dishes. Good for anyone staying or working around Ban Chang–Map Ta Phut who wants grilled meat close by without driving into town.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Most buffet spots get packed from around 8 pm onward, especially Friday and Saturday — if you're coming with a big group, calling ahead to book a table is safer. Many places also charge for drinks separately from the buffet: some bill drinks by the bottle, others do a 30–40 THB per-head refill. Ask before you sit down so the bill doesn't surprise you.

blocks.text: How to pick the right Rayong mookata spot

items: Tightest budget — aim for the 199 THB/head spots like Aroi Jaeng Riverside, 4 Mong, or Rama 9 Grilled Shrimp. Great value if you can eat a lot.
Into butter-grilled beef — Je Jai Dee's butter-grilled kho khun beef, or Tid Mun, which combines butter-grill, mookata, and shabu in one place.
Want seafood — Thao Kae in the Saeng Chan Beach area, and 4 Mong, both stand out for shrimp and seafood.
Not a buffet fan, want good cuts — CoCo Yakiniku for à la carte yakiniku, or Mana for both hot-pot dipping and grilling.
Staying around Ban Chang–Map Ta Phut — Ba Korean Grill is closer than the in-town spots, no need to drive into the city.

blocks.text: Eating Rayong mookata for value and safety

items.name: Start with grilled before fried
items.blurb: Grill pork, beef, and seafood until you're genuinely full first, then move on to snacks and dessert. It's better value than heading for the fried stuff right away.

items.name: Change the broth and clean the grill
items.blurb: If the broth gets cloudy or the grill is heavily burnt, ask to swap them — the taste improves and you grill cleaner. Most places are happy to change it for you.

faq.q: How much is mookata / BBQ buffet in Rayong per head?
faq.a: Most run 199–279 THB a head. Lighter-priced spots like Aroi Jaeng Riverside, 4 Mong, and Rama 9 Grilled Shrimp start around 199 THB, while Je Jai Dee and Tid Mun sit around 219–258 THB. Big shabu + grill lines like Mana move up to around 299–385 THB. Advertised prices often don't include drinks, so ask before you sit down.

faq.q: What time do Rayong BBQ buffet spots open?
faq.a: Most are dinner places, opening around 16:00 and closing 22:00–23:00. A few, like 4 Mong, open at 3 pm, while Korean BBQ spots in malls like Hankook Sikdang open earlier in the day. They usually get busy around 7–8 pm.

faq.q: Which spot is best for seafood at a grill buffet?
faq.a: Thao Kae Buffet in the Saeng Chan Beach area stands out for shrimp, shellfish, crab, and salmon, while 4 Mong and Rama 9 Grilled Shrimp also have fresh shrimp to refill — good for seafood lovers at a buffet price.

faq.q: Not a buffet fan — where can I get good grilled beef?
faq.a: Try CoCo Yakiniku, an à la carte yakiniku spot with several beef grades including grain-fed kho khun, Australian, and Thai wagyu — or Hankook Sikdang at Star IT Center for order-by-the-plate Korean BBQ.

faq.q: Staying around Ban Chang or Map Ta Phut — any grill spots nearby?
faq.a: Yes — Ba Korean Grill in the Ban Chang area is a set-menu Korean BBQ, closer than the in-town Rayong spots for anyone staying or working in that zone.
